content.title: About
content.content: Spaghetti Sauce with Seafood is a ready‑to‑use tomato sauce enriched with pieces of shrimp, mussels, calamari and fish. It is perfect for quick pasta, risotto or seafood dishes. The flavor combines the sweetness of tomatoes, a hint of garlic heat and the aroma of fresh marine delicacies.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tomatoes in the sauce undergo a short heat treatment to retain most of their vitamins.
Seafood pieces are usually pre‑seared, which intensifies their aroma.
In Italy similar sauces are called "sugo di mare" and are used in traditional coastal recipes.
The sauce may contain a small amount of white wine, adding depth to the taste.
Because natural ingredients are used, no artificial flavorings are required.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Seafood provides omega‑3s that support heart and vascular health.

items.title: High protein content
items.content: Shrimp, mussels and fish supply a complete set of amino acids beneficial for muscles and tissue repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Seafood is a source of vitamin B12 and niacin, important for the nervous system and metabolism.

items.title: Lycopene in tomatoes
items.content: Tomatoes are rich in lycopene, an antioxidant that may reduce the risk of certain chronic diseases.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Unlike cream‑based sauces, this product contains minimal saturated fat.

items.title: Seafood allergy
items.content: The product can trigger allergic reactions in individuals sensitive to crustaceans or mollusks.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: The sauce can be salty; people limiting sodium intake should monitor portion size.

items.title: Glutamate presence
items.content: Some recipes include added monosodium glutamate, which may cause sensitivity in certain consumers.

items.title: Post‑opening storage
items.content: After opening, keep the sauce refrigerated and consume within 3‑5 days.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Heat the sauce in a pan, add cooked spaghetti and stir. You can also toss in extra fresh seafood, herbs (parsley, basil) and a drizzle of olive oil. The sauce works well for casseroles, lasagna or as a base for risotto.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened sauce in a cool, dry place. Once opened, keep it in the refrigerator in an airtight container. Discard if the smell, color or texture changes or if mold appears.
